source.text: וְאַתָּ֤ה בֶן־אָדָם֙ קַח־לְךָ֣ לְבֵנָ֔ה וְנָתַתָּ֥ה אוֹתָ֖הּ לְפָנֶ֑יךָ וְחַקּוֹתָ֥ עָלֶ֛יהָ עִ֖יר אֶת־יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And you, son of man, take for yourself a brick and set it before you, and engrave on it a city, Jerusalem.

en.L: "And you, son of man, take for yourself a brick and set it before you, and engrave on it a city, Jerusalem.
en.B: "Now, son of man, take a clay brick, set it in front of you, and draw on it a city, Jerusalem.
en.R: "Son of man, take a clay brick and put it in front of you. Draw a picture of the city of Jerusalem on it.

pt.L: "E tu, filho do homem, toma para ti um tijolo e põe-no diante de ti, e grava nele uma cidade, Jerusalém.
pt.B: "Agora, filho do homem, pega um tijolo de barro, coloca-o diante de ti e desenha nele uma cidade, Jerusalém.
pt.R: "Filho do homem, pega um tijolo de barro e coloca-o na tua frente. Desenha nele a cidade de Jerusalém.

sw.L: "Nawe, mwana wa binadamu, jitwalie tofali, uliweke mbele yako, uchore juu yake mji, Yerusalemu.
sw.B: "Sasa, mwana wa binadamu, chukua tofali la udongo, uliweke mbele yako, uchore juu yake mji, Yerusalemu.
sw.R: "Mwana wa binadamu, chukua tofali la udongo uliweke mbele yako. Chora juu yake picha ya mji wa Yerusalemu.

ko.L: "그리고 너, 사람의 아들아, 너는 벽돌 하나를 가져다가 네 앞에 놓고, 그 위에 성읍, 곧 예루살렘을 새겨라.
ko.B: "이제 사람의 아들아, 너는 진흙 벽돌 하나를 가져다가 네 앞에 놓고, 그 위에 예루살렘 성읍을 그려라.
ko.R: "사람의 아들아, 진흙 벽돌 하나를 가져다가 네 앞에 놓아라. 그 위에 예루살렘 성의 그림을 그려라.

vi.L: "Và ngươi, hỡi con người, hãy lấy cho mình một viên gạch và đặt nó trước mặt ngươi, và khắc trên nó một thành, là Giê-ru-sa-lem.
vi.B: "Bây giờ, hỡi con người, hãy lấy một viên gạch bằng đất sét, đặt trước mặt con, và vẽ trên đó một thành, là Giê-ru-sa-lem.
vi.R: "Hỡi con người, hãy lấy một viên gạch bằng đất sét và đặt trước mặt con. Hãy vẽ hình thành Giê-ru-sa-lem lên trên đó.

fr.L: « Et toi, fils d’homme, prends-toi une brique, place-la devant toi, et grave sur elle une ville, Jérusalem.
fr.B: « Maintenant, fils d’homme, prends une brique d’argile, pose-la devant toi et dessine dessus une ville, Jérusalem.
fr.R: « Fils d’homme, prends une brique d’argile et pose-la devant toi. Dessine dessus la ville de Jérusalem.

es.L: «Y tú, hijo de hombre, toma para ti un ladrillo y ponlo delante de ti, y graba en él una ciudad, Jerusalén.
es.B: «Ahora, hijo de hombre, toma un ladrillo de barro, ponlo delante de ti y dibuja en él una ciudad, Jerusalén.
es.R: «Hijo de hombre, toma un ladrillo de barro y ponlo delante de ti. Dibuja en él la ciudad de Jerusalén.

decisions.choice: the sign-acts: the prophet acts out the message
decisions.reason: Chapters 4-5 are a series of signs that Ezekiel is to act out in front of the exiles: the city under siege (4:1-3), the prophet lying on his side (4:4-8), the starvation rations (4:9-17) and the shaving of his head and beard (5:1-4). Other prophets did the same: Isaiah walked naked and barefoot (Isaiah 20), Jeremiah buried a loincloth, broke a jar and wore a yoke (Jeremiah 13; 19; 27). A sign-act was more than a picture; it announced what the LORD was about to do. Here it portrays the siege of Jerusalem, which began in 588 BC, some five years after Ezekiel's call, and the exile that followed. 5:5-17 explains it.

decisions.choice: a brick ... engrave on it: a clay brick with a drawing scratched into it
decisions.reason: Bricks were made of clay and dried in the sun; while still soft, they could be marked. Babylonian scribes drew plans of buildings and cities on clay. Ezekiel's brick becomes a model of Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: And you: the LORD's speech goes on
decisions.reason: The chapter begins with "And you", carrying on the LORD's words to Ezekiel from 3:24-27. The quotation mark opens again at the chapter break, and the speech runs to the end of verse 12.

decisions.choice: engrave (L); draw (B, R)
decisions.reason: The verb means to cut or scratch a design into a surface. Balanced and Readable say "draw", since the point is the picture of the city. They say "clay brick" so that readers do not picture a fired modern brick.

source.text: וְנָתַתָּ֨ה עָלֶ֜יהָ מָצ֗וֹר וּבָנִ֤יתָ עָלֶ֨יהָ֙ דָּיֵ֔ק וְשָׁפַכְתָּ֥ עָלֶ֖יהָ סֹֽלְלָ֑ה וְנָתַתָּ֨ה עָלֶ֧יהָ מַחֲנ֛וֹת וְשִׂים־עָלֶ֥יהָ כָּרִ֖ים סָבִֽיב׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will put on it a siege, and build against it a siege wall, and pour out against it a ramp, and set against it camps, and place against it battering rams all around.

en.L: And you will put a siege against it, and build against it a siege wall, and pour out against it a ramp, and set against it camps, and place against it battering rams all around.
en.B: Lay siege to it: build a siege wall against it, heap up a ramp against it, set up army camps around it, and place battering rams against it on every side.
en.R: Then act out an attack on the city. Build siege walls around it, and pile up a dirt ramp against it. Set up army camps, and put battering rams all around it.

pt.L: E porás contra ela um cerco, e edificarás contra ela uma muralha de cerco, e levantarás contra ela uma rampa, e porás contra ela acampamentos, e colocarás contra ela aríetes ao redor.
pt.B: Põe a cidade sob cerco: constrói contra ela uma muralha de cerco, levanta contra ela uma rampa, monta acampamentos de exército ao redor dela e coloca aríetes contra ela por todos os lados.
pt.R: Depois representa um ataque contra a cidade. Constrói muralhas de cerco ao redor dela e amontoa uma rampa de terra contra ela. Monta acampamentos de exército e coloca aríetes em volta de toda a cidade.

sw.L: Nawe utauzingira, na kujenga ukuta wa kuuzingira, na kumwaga boma la udongo dhidi yake, na kuweka kambi dhidi yake, na kuweka magogo ya kubomolea dhidi yake pande zote.
sw.B: Uuzingire: jenga ukuta wa kuuzingira, lundika boma la udongo dhidi yake, simika kambi za jeshi kuuzunguka, na uweke magogo ya kubomolea dhidi yake pande zote.
sw.R: Kisha uigize jinsi jeshi linavyoushambulia mji. Jenga kuta za kuuzingira, na ulundike boma la udongo dhidi yake. Weka kambi za jeshi, na magogo ya kubomolea kuta pande zote kuuzunguka.

ko.L: 그리고 너는 그것에 포위망을 치고, 그것을 향해 포위벽을 쌓고, 그것을 향해 흙 언덕을 쏟아 쌓고, 그것을 향해 진을 치고, 그것을 향해 둘레에 성벽 부수는 망치를 세워라.
ko.B: 그 성읍을 포위하여라. 그 성을 향해 포위벽을 쌓고, 흙 언덕을 쌓아 올리고, 그 둘레에 군대의 진을 치고, 사방에 성벽 부수는 망치를 세워라.
ko.R: 그런 다음 그 성을 공격하는 시늉을 하여라. 성 둘레에 포위벽을 쌓고, 성벽에 맞대어 흙 언덕을 쌓아 올려라. 군대의 진을 치고, 성 둘레에 성벽 부수는 망치를 세워라.

vi.L: Và ngươi sẽ đặt cuộc vây hãm nghịch cùng nó, xây tường vây hãm nghịch cùng nó, đắp ụ đất nghịch cùng nó, đóng các trại quân nghịch cùng nó, và đặt các đòn phá thành chung quanh nghịch cùng nó.
vi.B: Hãy vây hãm thành ấy: xây tường vây quanh, đắp ụ đất tấn công, đóng các trại quân chung quanh, và đặt các đòn phá thành khắp các phía.
vi.R: Rồi hãy diễn lại cảnh tấn công thành ấy. Hãy xây tường vây quanh thành và đắp một ụ đất sát tường thành. Hãy dựng các trại quân, và đặt các đòn phá thành khắp chung quanh.

fr.L: Et tu mettras contre elle un siège, et tu bâtiras contre elle un mur de siège, et tu dresseras contre elle une rampe, et tu placeras contre elle des camps, et tu disposeras contre elle des béliers tout autour.
fr.B: Assiège-la : bâtis contre elle un mur de siège, élève contre elle une rampe, installe des camps autour d’elle et dispose des béliers contre elle de tous côtés.
fr.R: Ensuite, fais comme si une armée attaquait la ville. Construis des murs de siège autour d’elle, et entasse de la terre contre elle pour faire une rampe. Installe des camps militaires, et mets tout autour des machines pour enfoncer les murs.

es.L: Y pondrás contra ella un asedio, y edificarás contra ella un muro de asedio, y levantarás contra ella una rampa, y pondrás contra ella campamentos, y colocarás contra ella arietes alrededor.
es.B: Pon sitio a la ciudad: construye contra ella un muro de asedio, levanta contra ella una rampa, instala campamentos a su alrededor y coloca arietes contra ella por todos lados.
es.R: Luego representa un ataque contra la ciudad. Construye muros de asedio a su alrededor y amontona tierra para hacer una rampa contra ella. Instala campamentos de soldados y pon arietes alrededor de ella.

decisions.choice: siege wall, ramp, camps and battering rams: the works of a siege army
decisions.reason: These are the methods of ancient siege warfare. The siege wall shut the city in and gave the attackers towers to shoot from (2 Kings 25:1); the ramp was a slope of earth and stones piled against the city wall so that the battering rams could be brought up to it (2 Samuel 20:15; Jeremiah 6:6). Assyrian palace carvings of the siege of Lachish show all of them. Ezekiel is to build a model of them around his brick.

decisions.choice: you will put a siege against it: Ezekiel plays the besieger
decisions.reason: Ezekiel takes the part of the enemy army; verse 3 shows that in doing so he stands for the LORD himself, who is bringing the siege on his own city (5:8).

decisions.choice: act out an attack on the city (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly that Ezekiel is acting out the siege with a model. It says "dirt ramp" for the ramp of earth (m1).

decisions.choice: "des béliers" (Literal, Balanced); "des machines pour enfoncer les murs" (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Bélier" is the French word for a battering ram, but it is also the animal; Readable describes the machine so a young reader is not misled.

source.text: וְאַתָּ֤ה קַח־לְךָ֙ מַחֲבַ֣ת בַּרְזֶ֔ל וְנָתַתָּ֤ה אוֹתָהּ֙ קִ֣יר בַּרְזֶ֔ל בֵּינְךָ֖ וּבֵ֣ין הָעִ֑יר וַהֲכִינֹתָה֩ אֶת־פָּנֶ֨יךָ אֵלֶ֜יהָ וְהָיְתָ֤ה בַמָּצוֹר֙ וְצַרְתָּ֣ עָלֶ֔יהָ א֥וֹת הִ֖יא לְבֵ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And you, take for yourself a griddle of iron, and you will make it a wall of iron between you and the city, and you will direct your face toward it, and it will be in siege, and you will besiege it; a sign it [is] for [the] house of Israel.

en.L: And you, take for yourself an iron griddle, and set it [as] an iron wall between you and the city; and direct your face toward it, and it will be under siege, and you will besiege it. This [is] a sign for the house of Israel.
en.B: Then take an iron griddle and set it up as an iron wall between you and the city. Turn to face it. It will be under siege, and you will besiege it. This is a sign for the house of Israel.
en.R: Then take an iron baking pan and set it up like an iron wall between you and the city. Turn toward the city. It will be under attack, and you will be the one attacking it. This will be a sign for the people of Israel.

pt.L: E tu, toma para ti uma chapa de ferro, e põe-na [como] um muro de ferro entre ti e a cidade; e dirige o teu rosto para ela, e ela estará sob cerco, e tu a sitiarás. Isto [é] um sinal para a casa de Israel.
pt.B: Depois pega uma chapa de ferro e coloca-a como um muro de ferro entre ti e a cidade. Volta o rosto para ela. Ela estará sob cerco, e tu a sitiarás. Isto é um sinal para a casa de Israel.
pt.R: Depois pega uma chapa de ferro de assar pão e coloca-a como um muro de ferro entre ti e a cidade. Vira-te para a cidade. Ela estará sendo atacada, e tu serás quem a ataca. Isto será um sinal para o povo de Israel.

sw.L: Nawe jitwalie kikaango cha chuma, ukiweke [kama] ukuta wa chuma kati yako na mji; nawe ukaze uso wako kuuelekea, nao utakuwa umezingirwa, nawe utauzingira. Hii [ni] ishara kwa nyumba ya Israeli.
sw.B: Kisha chukua kikaango cha chuma ukisimamishe kama ukuta wa chuma kati yako na mji. Geuka uuelekee. Utakuwa umezingirwa, nawe utauzingira. Hii ni ishara kwa nyumba ya Israeli.
sw.R: Kisha chukua kikaango cha chuma ukisimamishe kama ukuta wa chuma kati yako na mji. Geuka uuelekee mji. Utakuwa unashambuliwa, nawe utakuwa ndiye unayeushambulia. Hii itakuwa ishara kwa watu wa Israeli.

ko.L: 그리고 너는 철판 하나를 가져다가 너와 성읍 사이에 철벽으로 세우고, 네 얼굴을 그 성읍으로 향하여라. 그러면 그것이 포위될 것이니, 너는 그것을 포위하여라. 이것이 이스라엘 집에 표징이다.
ko.B: 또 철판 하나를 가져다가 너와 성읍 사이에 철벽처럼 세워라. 그리고 그 성읍을 마주 보고 서라. 그 성읍은 포위될 것이고, 너는 그 성읍을 포위할 것이다. 이것이 이스라엘 집에 주는 표징이다.
ko.R: 그리고 쇠로 된 빵 굽는 판을 가져다가 너와 성 사이에 쇠벽처럼 세워라. 그 성 쪽으로 돌아서라. 그 성은 공격을 받을 것이고, 너는 그 성을 공격하는 사람이 될 것이다. 이것이 이스라엘 백성에게 표징이 될 것이다.

vi.L: Và ngươi, hãy lấy cho mình một cái chảo sắt, và đặt nó [làm] một bức tường sắt giữa ngươi và thành; và hãy xây mặt ngươi về phía nó, và nó sẽ bị vây hãm, và ngươi sẽ vây hãm nó. Đây [là] một dấu hiệu cho nhà Y-sơ-ra-ên.
vi.B: Rồi hãy lấy một cái chảo sắt và dựng nó lên làm một bức tường sắt giữa con và thành. Hãy quay mặt về phía thành. Thành sẽ bị vây hãm, và con sẽ vây hãm nó. Đây là một dấu hiệu cho nhà Y-sơ-ra-ên.
vi.R: Rồi hãy lấy một cái chảo nướng bằng sắt và dựng nó lên như một bức tường sắt giữa con và thành. Hãy quay về phía thành. Thành sẽ bị tấn công, và chính con là người tấn công nó. Đây sẽ là một dấu hiệu cho dân Y-sơ-ra-ên.

fr.L: Et toi, prends-toi une plaque de fer, et mets-la [comme] un mur de fer entre toi et la ville ; et tourne ta face vers elle, et elle sera assiégée, et tu l’assiégeras. C’[est] un signe pour la maison d’Israël.
fr.B: Puis prends une plaque de fer et dresse-la comme un mur de fer entre toi et la ville. Tourne ton regard vers elle. Elle sera assiégée, et c’est toi qui l’assiégeras. C’est un signe pour la maison d’Israël.
fr.R: Puis prends une plaque de cuisson en fer et dresse-la comme un mur de fer entre toi et la ville. Tourne-toi vers la ville. Elle sera attaquée, et c’est toi qui l’attaqueras. Ce sera un signe pour le peuple d’Israël.

es.L: Y tú, toma para ti una plancha de hierro, y ponla [como] muro de hierro entre ti y la ciudad; y pon tu rostro hacia ella, y estará sitiada, y tú la sitiarás. Esto [es] una señal para la casa de Israel.
es.B: Luego toma una plancha de hierro y colócala como un muro de hierro entre ti y la ciudad. Vuélvete de cara a ella. Estará sitiada, y tú la sitiarás. Esto es una señal para la casa de Israel.
es.R: Después toma una plancha de hierro para cocinar y colócala como un muro de hierro entre ti y la ciudad. Vuélvete hacia la ciudad. Estará bajo ataque, y tú serás quien la ataque. Esto será una señal para el pueblo de Israel.

decisions.choice: an iron griddle as an iron wall: a barrier that cannot be broken
alternatives: the barrier between the LORD and the city
decisions.reason: The word is the flat iron plate on which bread was baked (Leviticus 2:5). Set between Ezekiel and the city, it becomes a wall of iron. It may stand for the siege wall that nothing can get through, or for the barrier between the LORD and the city, which he will not lift: Lamentations 3:44 says, "You have covered yourself with a cloud so that no prayer can pass through".

decisions.choice: direct your face toward it: fix your gaze on it in hostility
decisions.reason: The verb means to set or fix; with "face" it means to turn one's whole attention to something. In Ezekiel the face set toward a place is a sign of hostility and judgment (verse 7; 6:2; 13:17; 14:8). See the note at 6:2, where a related phrase is used.

decisions.choice: a sign: an act that shows what is coming
decisions.reason: A sign is something seen that points to something else and guarantees it. Ezekiel's actions are signs of what will happen to Jerusalem (12:6, 11; 24:24, 27); Isaiah's walking naked was a sign in the same way (Isaiah 20:3).

decisions.choice: direct your face toward it (L); turn to face it (B); turn toward (R)
decisions.reason: The verb here, "fix" or "direct", is not the one in the phrase "set your face toward" (6:2), but the sense is close, so Balanced and Readable follow the wording set for that phrase in Ezekiel. Literal says "direct" to keep the two verbs apart. Readable says "baking pan" for the griddle.

decisions.choice: um sinal (every level)
decisions.reason: For the whole book (4:3; 12:6, 11; 14:8; 24:24, 27): the acted signs (m3) are "sinal" at every level, the word Isaiah 20:3 uses in Portuguese for the prophet's acted sign; "símbolo" would lose the sense that the sign guarantees what is coming. God's commands to Ezekiel in the sign-acts (4-5; 12) use the "tu" imperative at every level ("pega", "coloca", "deita-te"), with the forms Brazilians use ("faz", "diz").

decisions.choice: uma chapa de ferro (L, B); uma chapa de ferro de assar pão (R)
decisions.reason: The griddle (m1) is a flat iron plate for baking bread, which Brazilian Portuguese calls "chapa"; Readable says what it was for, as the English Readable says "baking pan". "Panela" and "assadeira" would picture a pot or a tray with sides.

decisions.choice: kaza uso wako kuelekea (L); geuka uelekee (B, R)
decisions.reason: Ezekiel's "set your face toward" keeps the Literal wording of the published Jeremiah 44:11 and Luke 9:51, and Balanced and Readable say plainly "turn to face", as the terms note sets it for the whole book. "Ishara" for a sign, as in John.

decisions.choice: "네 얼굴을 ~로 향하여라" (L); "~을 마주 보고 서라" (B); "~ 쪽으로 돌아서라" (R)
decisions.reason: The term sheet's wording for setting the face toward something, used for the formula through the book.

decisions.choice: "표징" (sign)
decisions.reason: "표징" is the word the published Korean Genesis 9:13 and the prophets use for a sign given by God; "표적" stays the Gospel word for Jesus's signs.

decisions.choice: hãy xây mặt ngươi về phía (L); hãy quay mặt về phía (B); hãy quay về phía (R)
decisions.reason: The idiom "set your face toward" is kept in one wording per level through Ezekiel, with "nghịch cùng" where the Hebrew has "against". A city is "nó".

decisions.choice: "tourne ta face vers" (Literal); "tourne ton regard vers" (Balanced); "tourne-toi vers" (Readable), for the whole book
decisions.reason: The term sheet's three wordings for this idiom (and for "set your face toward" in 6:2 and later), matching the English.

decisions.choice: "pon tu rostro hacia" (L); "vuélvete de cara a" (B); "vuélvete hacia" (R)
decisions.reason: Book-wide levels for setting or directing the face toward a place or people

decisions.choice: "una plancha de hierro"
decisions.reason: The flat baking plate of 1 Chronicles 23:29 in Spanish; R adds "para cocinar"

source.text: וְאַתָּ֤ה שְׁכַב֙ עַל־צִדְּךָ֣ הַשְּׂמָאלִ֔י וְשַׂמְתָּ֛ אֶת־עֲוֺ֥ן בֵּֽית־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל עָלָ֑יו מִסְפַּ֤ר הַיָּמִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תִּשְׁכַּ֣ב עָלָ֔יו תִּשָּׂ֖א אֶת־עֲוֺנָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And you, lie on your side the left, and put the iniquity of [the] house of Israel on it; [the] number of the days which you lie on it, you will bear their iniquity.

en.L: And you, lie on your left side, and put the iniquity of the house of Israel upon it; [for] the number of the days that you lie on it, you will bear their iniquity.
en.B: Then lie on your left side and lay the guilt of the house of Israel on it. For the number of days that you lie on that side, you will bear their guilt.
en.R: Then lie down on your left side and lay the sin of the people of Israel on yourself. For each day you lie on your side, you will carry the punishment for their sin.

pt.L: E tu, deita-te sobre o teu lado esquerdo, e põe sobre ele a iniquidade da casa de Israel; [pelo] número dos dias em que te deitares sobre ele, levarás a iniquidade deles.
pt.B: Depois deita-te sobre o lado esquerdo e põe sobre ele a culpa da casa de Israel. Pelo número de dias em que ficares deitado sobre esse lado, carregarás a culpa deles.
pt.R: Depois deita-te sobre o teu lado esquerdo e coloca sobre ti o pecado do povo de Israel. Para cada dia que ficares deitado de lado, carregarás o castigo pelo pecado deles.

sw.L: Nawe lala upande wako wa kushoto, uweke uovu wa nyumba ya Israeli juu yake; [kwa] hesabu ya siku utakazolala juu yake, utabeba uovu wao.
sw.B: Kisha ulale upande wako wa kushoto na kuweka hatia ya nyumba ya Israeli juu yake. Kwa hesabu ya siku utakazolala upande huo, utabeba hatia yao.
sw.R: Kisha ulale chini kwa upande wako wa kushoto, ujitwike dhambi ya watu wa Israeli. Kwa kila siku utakayolala kwa upande huo, utabeba adhabu ya dhambi yao.

ko.L: 그리고 너는 네 왼쪽으로 누워서 이스라엘 집의 죄악을 그 위에 두어라. 네가 그쪽으로 누워 있는 날 수만큼 너는 그들의 죄악을 짊어질 것이다.
ko.B: 그다음에 너는 왼쪽으로 누워서 이스라엘 집의 죄를 그 위에 얹어라. 네가 그쪽으로 누워 있는 날 수만큼 너는 그들의 죄를 짊어질 것이다.
ko.R: 그다음에 왼쪽으로 누워서 이스라엘 백성의 죄를 네 몸에 얹어라. 네가 그렇게 누워 있는 날마다 너는 그들의 죄에 대한 벌을 짊어질 것이다.

vi.L: Và ngươi, hãy nằm nghiêng bên trái, và đặt tội ác của nhà Y-sơ-ra-ên trên đó; ngươi nằm trên đó bao nhiêu ngày, ngươi sẽ mang tội ác của chúng bấy nhiêu ngày.
vi.B: Rồi hãy nằm nghiêng bên trái và đặt tội lỗi của nhà Y-sơ-ra-ên lên bên ấy. Con nằm nghiêng bên ấy bao nhiêu ngày thì con sẽ mang tội lỗi của chúng bấy nhiêu ngày.
vi.R: Rồi hãy nằm nghiêng bên trái và đặt tội của dân Y-sơ-ra-ên lên chính mình. Mỗi ngày con nằm nghiêng như vậy, con sẽ gánh hình phạt cho tội của chúng.

fr.L: Et toi, couche-toi sur ton côté gauche, et mets sur lui l’iniquité de la maison d’Israël ; [pendant] le nombre de jours où tu seras couché sur lui, tu porteras leur iniquité.
fr.B: Puis couche-toi sur le côté gauche et mets sur ce côté la faute de la maison d’Israël. Pendant autant de jours que tu resteras couché sur ce côté, tu porteras leur faute.
fr.R: Ensuite, couche-toi sur le côté gauche et prends sur toi le péché du peuple d’Israël. Chaque jour où tu resteras couché sur le côté, tu porteras la punition de leur péché.

es.L: Y tú, acuéstate sobre tu lado izquierdo, y pon sobre él la iniquidad de la casa de Israel; [por] el número de los días que estés acostado sobre él, llevarás su iniquidad.
es.B: Luego acuéstate sobre tu lado izquierdo y pon sobre él la culpa de la casa de Israel. Durante el número de días que estés acostado sobre ese lado, cargarás con su culpa.
es.R: Luego acuéstate sobre tu lado izquierdo y pon sobre ti el pecado del pueblo de Israel. Por cada día que estés acostado sobre ese lado, cargarás con el castigo de su pecado.

decisions.choice: bear their iniquity: carry the guilt and its punishment
decisions.reason: The word for iniquity means both the wrong and the guilt and punishment that follow it. To "bear iniquity" is to suffer the consequence of sin, as Israel bore its iniquity for forty years in the wilderness, a year for each day (Numbers 14:34). Ezekiel does not take away the people's sin by lying on his side; he acts out the length of their punishment.

decisions.choice: the left side ... the house of Israel: perhaps the northern kingdom
decisions.reason: Facing east, as the Hebrews did to name the directions, the left hand is north and the right hand south. So the left side may stand for the northern kingdom of Israel, and the right side for Judah in the south (verse 6). Elsewhere in Ezekiel "the house of Israel" means the whole people, and it may do so here too.

decisions.choice: lie on your side: for part of each day
decisions.reason: Ezekiel also prepares and eats his food during these days (verses 9-12), so he probably lay on his side for part of each day, in public view, rather than without a break.

decisions.choice: iniquity (L); guilt (B); sin, punishment for sin (R)
decisions.reason: *'Awon* is "iniquity" at Literal, "guilt" or "sin" at Balanced and "sin" at Readable, as in Isaiah. Balanced says "guilt" here because the verse is about bearing it. Readable says "carry the punishment for their sin", which is what bearing iniquity means (m1).

decisions.choice: a iniquidade (L); a culpa or o pecado (B); o pecado, o castigo pelo pecado (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book: 'awon (m1) is "iniquidade" at Literal, the Old Testament terms' word, and at Balanced and Readable follows the English level, "culpa" where the verse is about bearing it and "pecado" elsewhere; Readable says "carregar o castigo pelo pecado" for "bear iniquity", as the English Readable does (r-en-1).

decisions.choice: uovu (L); hatia (B); dhambi, adhabu ya dhambi (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word means both the wrong and the guilt and punishment it brings (meaning decision); each level follows the English choice, "uovu" as in the published Leviticus 26:39 at Literal and "hatia" at Balanced.

decisions.choice: tội ác (L); tội lỗi (B); tội, hình phạt cho tội (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word covers the wrong and the guilt and punishment it brings; Readable spells out the punishment, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "llevar la iniquidad" (L); "cargar con la culpa" (B); "cargar con el castigo de su pecado" (R)
decisions.reason: As Leviticus in Spanish (llevará la iniquidad; cargará con su culpa)

source.text: וַאֲנִ֗י נָתַ֤תִּֽי לְךָ֙ אֶת־שְׁנֵ֣י עֲוֺנָ֔ם לְמִסְפַּ֣ר יָמִ֔ים שְׁלֹשׁ־מֵא֥וֹת וְתִשְׁעִ֖ים י֑וֹם וְנָשָׂ֖אתָ עֲוֺ֥ן בֵּֽית־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And I have assigned to you the years of their iniquity to [the] number of days, three hundred and ninety days; and you will bear [the] iniquity of [the] house of Israel.

en.L: And I have assigned to you the years of their iniquity as a number of days, 390 days; and you will bear the iniquity of the house of Israel.
en.B: I have assigned you a number of days equal to the years of their guilt, 390 days. So you will bear the guilt of the house of Israel.
en.R: I have given you one day for each year of their sin: 390 days. For that long you will carry the punishment for the sin of the people of Israel.

pt.L: E eu te designei os anos da iniquidade deles como um número de dias, 390 dias; e levarás a iniquidade da casa de Israel.
pt.B: Eu te designei um número de dias igual aos anos da culpa deles: 390 dias. Assim carregarás a culpa da casa de Israel.
pt.R: Eu te dei um dia para cada ano do pecado deles: 390 dias. Durante todo esse tempo carregarás o castigo pelo pecado do povo de Israel.

sw.L: Nami nimekupangia miaka ya uovu wao kuwa hesabu ya siku, siku 390; nawe utabeba uovu wa nyumba ya Israeli.
sw.B: Nimekupangia hesabu ya siku sawa na miaka ya hatia yao, siku 390. Hivyo utaibeba hatia ya nyumba ya Israeli.
sw.R: Nimekupa siku moja kwa kila mwaka wa dhambi yao: siku 390. Kwa muda huo wote utabeba adhabu ya dhambi ya watu wa Israeli.

ko.L: 그리고 내가 그들의 죄악의 햇수를 날 수로 너에게 정해 주었으니, 곧 390일이다. 너는 이스라엘 집의 죄악을 짊어질 것이다.
ko.B: 내가 그들이 죄를 지은 햇수만큼의 날 수, 곧 390일을 너에게 정해 주었다. 그렇게 너는 이스라엘 집의 죄를 짊어질 것이다.
ko.R: 나는 그들이 죄를 지은 한 해를 하루로 쳐서 너에게 390일을 주었다. 그 기간 동안 너는 이스라엘 백성의 죄에 대한 벌을 짊어질 것이다.

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã định cho ngươi số năm tội ác của chúng thành số ngày, 390 ngày; và ngươi sẽ mang tội ác của nhà Y-sơ-ra-ên.
vi.B: Ta đã định cho con số ngày bằng số năm tội lỗi của chúng, tức là 390 ngày. Như vậy con sẽ mang tội lỗi của nhà Y-sơ-ra-ên.
vi.R: Ta đã cho con một ngày cho mỗi năm chúng phạm tội: 390 ngày. Suốt thời gian ấy con sẽ gánh hình phạt cho tội của dân Y-sơ-ra-ên.

fr.L: Et moi, je t’ai assigné les années de leur iniquité en un nombre de jours : 390 jours ; et tu porteras l’iniquité de la maison d’Israël.
fr.B: Je t’ai fixé un nombre de jours égal aux années de leur faute : 390 jours. Ainsi tu porteras la faute de la maison d’Israël.
fr.R: Je t’ai donné un jour pour chaque année de leur péché : 390 jours. Pendant tout ce temps, tu porteras la punition du péché du peuple d’Israël.

es.L: Y yo te he asignado los años de su iniquidad como número de días, 390 días; y llevarás la iniquidad de la casa de Israel.
es.B: Te he asignado un número de días igual a los años de su culpa: 390 días. Así cargarás con la culpa de la casa de Israel.
es.R: Te he dado un día por cada año de su pecado: 390 días. Durante ese tiempo cargarás con el castigo del pecado del pueblo de Israel.

decisions.choice: 390 days: the Hebrew number; the Greek translation has 190
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text has 390 days here and in verse 9. The Greek translation reads 190 in both places, and in verse 4 adds that Ezekiel lies on his left side 150 days. Neither number is explained in the text. The 390 years may count from the building of Solomon's temple, or from the division of the kingdom after Solomon, down to the fall of Jerusalem; added to the forty of verse 6, they make 430, the years of Israel in Egypt (Exodus 12:40). The 190 of the Greek may count from the fall of the northern kingdom. The Hebrew number is followed.

decisions.choice: the years ... as a number of days: a day for each year
decisions.reason: Each day Ezekiel lies on his side stands for a year of punishment, as in Numbers 14:34. Verse 6 says so in so many words.

decisions.choice: 390, in numerals (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: Numbers over ninety-nine are written in numerals at every level, as the style guide sets.

source.text: וְכִלִּיתָ֣ אֶת־אֵ֗לֶּה וְשָׁ֨כַבְתָּ֜ עַל־צִדְּךָ֤ הַיְמָנִי֙שֵׁנִ֔ית וְנָשָׂ֖אתָ אֶת־עֲוֺ֣ן בֵּית־יְהוּדָ֑ה אַרְבָּעִ֣ים י֔וֹם י֧וֹם לַשָּׁנָ֛ה י֥וֹם לַשָּׁנָ֖ה נְתַתִּ֥יו לָֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will complete these, and you will lie on your side the right a second [time], and you will bear [the] iniquity of [the] house of Judah forty days; a day for the year, a day for the year I have assigned it to you.

en.L: And when you have completed these, you will lie down a second [time], on your right side, and you will bear the iniquity of the house of Judah forty days; a day for a year, a day for a year I have assigned it to you.
en.B: When you have completed these days, lie down again, this time on your right side, and bear the guilt of the house of Judah for forty days. I have assigned you one day for each year.
en.R: When you have finished those days, lie down again, this time on your right side. For forty days you will carry the punishment for the sin of the people of Judah. I have given you one day for each year.

pt.L: E quando tiveres completado estes, te deitarás uma segunda [vez], sobre o teu lado direito, e levarás a iniquidade da casa de Judá quarenta dias; um dia por um ano, um dia por um ano eu te designei.
pt.B: Quando tiveres completado esses dias, deita-te de novo, desta vez sobre o lado direito, e carrega a culpa da casa de Judá por quarenta dias. Eu te designei um dia para cada ano.
pt.R: Quando tiveres terminado esses dias, deita-te de novo, desta vez sobre o lado direito. Durante quarenta dias carregarás o castigo pelo pecado do povo de Judá. Eu te dei um dia para cada ano.

sw.L: Nawe utakapozimaliza hizo, utalala mara ya pili, upande wako wa kuume, nawe utabeba uovu wa nyumba ya Yuda siku arobaini; siku kwa mwaka, siku kwa mwaka nimekupangia.
sw.B: Utakapozimaliza siku hizo, ulale tena, mara hii kwa upande wako wa kulia, uibebe hatia ya nyumba ya Yuda kwa siku arobaini. Nimekupangia siku moja kwa kila mwaka.
sw.R: Utakapozimaliza siku hizo, ulale tena, mara hii kwa upande wako wa kulia. Kwa siku arobaini utabeba adhabu ya dhambi ya watu wa Yuda. Nimekupa siku moja kwa kila mwaka.

ko.L: 그리고 네가 이것들을 마치면, 두 번째로 네 오른쪽으로 누워서 유다 집의 죄악을 사십 일 동안 짊어져라. 한 해에 하루, 한 해에 하루씩 내가 너에게 정해 주었다.
ko.B: 이 날들을 다 채우면, 이번에는 오른쪽으로 다시 누워서 유다 집의 죄를 사십 일 동안 짊어져라. 나는 한 해를 하루로 쳐서 너에게 정해 주었다.
ko.R: 그 날들이 다 끝나면, 이번에는 오른쪽으로 다시 누워라. 너는 사십 일 동안 유다 백성의 죄에 대한 벌을 짊어질 것이다. 나는 한 해를 하루로 쳐서 너에게 주었다.

vi.L: Và khi ngươi đã làm trọn những ngày ấy, ngươi sẽ nằm [lần] thứ hai, nghiêng bên phải, và ngươi sẽ mang tội ác của nhà Giu-đa bốn mươi ngày; một ngày cho một năm, một ngày cho một năm {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã định cho ngươi.
vi.B: Khi con đã làm trọn những ngày ấy, hãy nằm xuống lần nữa, lần này nghiêng bên phải, và mang tội lỗi của nhà Giu-đa trong bốn mươi ngày. Ta đã định cho con một ngày cho mỗi năm.
vi.R: Khi con đã xong những ngày ấy, hãy nằm xuống lần nữa, lần này nghiêng bên phải. Trong bốn mươi ngày, con sẽ gánh hình phạt cho tội của dân Giu-đa. Ta đã cho con một ngày cho mỗi năm.

fr.L: Et quand tu auras achevé ceux-ci, tu te coucheras une seconde [fois], sur ton côté droit, et tu porteras l’iniquité de la maison de Juda quarante jours ; un jour pour une année, un jour pour une année, je te l’ai assigné.
fr.B: Quand tu auras achevé ces jours, couche-toi de nouveau, cette fois sur le côté droit, et porte la faute de la maison de Juda pendant quarante jours. Je t’ai fixé un jour pour chaque année.
fr.R: Quand tu auras fini ces jours-là, couche-toi de nouveau, cette fois sur le côté droit. Pendant quarante jours, tu porteras la punition du péché du peuple de Juda. Je t’ai donné un jour pour chaque année.

es.L: Y cuando hayas cumplido estos, te acostarás por segunda vez, sobre tu lado derecho, y llevarás la iniquidad de la casa de Judá cuarenta días; un día por un año, un día por un año te lo he asignado.
es.B: Cuando hayas cumplido estos días, acuéstate otra vez, ahora sobre tu lado derecho, y carga con la culpa de la casa de Judá durante cuarenta días. Te he asignado un día por cada año.
es.R: Cuando hayas terminado esos días, acuéstate otra vez, ahora sobre tu lado derecho. Durante cuarenta días cargarás con el castigo del pecado del pueblo de Judá. Te he dado un día por cada año.

decisions.choice: your right side: the reading tradition
decisions.reason: The written consonants of "right" differ slightly in spelling from the form the scribes' marginal note tells the reader to say. The meaning is the same; the marginal reading is followed.

decisions.choice: forty days, a day for a year: a generation of punishment
decisions.reason: Forty years is the length of a generation, and of Israel's punishment in the wilderness (Numbers 14:33-34). Egypt too is to lie desolate forty years (29:11-13). The number gives Judah's exile the length of a lifetime, not an exact count of years.

decisions.choice: one day for each year (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the repeated "a day for a year, a day for a year". Balanced and Readable say it once, plainly. "Lie down again" gives "a second time".

source.text: וְאֶל־מְצ֤וֹר יְרוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ תָּכִ֣ין פָּנֶ֔יךָ וּֽזְרֹעֲךָ֖ חֲשׂוּפָ֑ה וְנִבֵּאתָ֖ עָלֶֽיהָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And toward the siege of Jerusalem you will direct your face, and your arm [will be] bared, and you will prophesy against it.

en.L: And toward the siege of Jerusalem you will direct your face, with your arm bared, and you will prophesy against it.
en.B: Turn to face the siege of Jerusalem with your arm bared, and prophesy against the city.
en.R: Turn toward Jerusalem, the city under attack. With your arm bare and ready for action, prophesy against it.

pt.L: E para o cerco de Jerusalém dirigirás o teu rosto, com o teu braço descoberto, e profetizarás contra ela.
pt.B: Volta o rosto para o cerco de Jerusalém, com o braço descoberto, e profetiza contra a cidade.
pt.R: Vira-te para Jerusalém, a cidade atacada. Com o braço descoberto e pronto para agir, profetiza contra ela.

sw.L: Nawe utakaza uso wako kuelekea kuzingirwa kwa Yerusalemu, mkono wako ukiwa wazi, nawe utatabiri dhidi yake.
sw.B: Geuka uelekee Yerusalemu uliozingirwa, mkono wako ukiwa wazi, na utabiri dhidi ya mji huo.
sw.R: Geuka uelekee Yerusalemu, mji unaoshambuliwa. Mkono wako ukiwa wazi na tayari kwa kazi, tabiri dhidi yake.

ko.L: 그리고 너는 예루살렘의 포위 쪽으로 네 얼굴을 향하고, 네 팔을 걷어붙이고, 그 성을 향해 예언하여라.
ko.B: 포위당한 예루살렘을 마주 보고 서서, 팔을 걷어붙이고 그 성을 향해 예언하여라.
ko.R: 공격을 받고 있는 예루살렘 쪽으로 돌아서라. 언제라도 칠 듯이 팔을 걷어붙이고, 그 성을 향해 예언하여라.

vi.L: Và ngươi sẽ xây mặt ngươi về phía cuộc vây hãm Giê-ru-sa-lem, với cánh tay để trần, và ngươi sẽ nói tiên tri nghịch cùng nó.
vi.B: Hãy quay mặt về phía Giê-ru-sa-lem đang bị vây hãm, với cánh tay để trần, và nói tiên tri nghịch cùng thành ấy.
vi.R: Hãy quay về phía Giê-ru-sa-lem, là thành đang bị tấn công. Với cánh tay để trần, sẵn sàng hành động, hãy truyền sứ điệp của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nghịch cùng thành ấy.

fr.L: Et vers le siège de Jérusalem tu tourneras ta face, le bras découvert, et tu prophétiseras contre elle.
fr.B: Tourne ton regard vers le siège de Jérusalem, le bras nu, et prophétise contre la ville.
fr.R: Tourne-toi vers Jérusalem, la ville attaquée. Le bras nu et prêt à agir, prophétise contre elle.

es.L: Y hacia el asedio de Jerusalén pondrás tu rostro, con tu brazo descubierto, y profetizarás contra ella.
es.B: Vuélvete de cara al asedio de Jerusalén, con el brazo descubierto, y profetiza contra la ciudad.
es.R: Vuélvete hacia Jerusalén, la ciudad atacada. Con el brazo descubierto y listo para actuar, profetiza contra ella.

decisions.choice: your arm bared: ready to strike
decisions.reason: To bare the arm is to push back the sleeve, ready for action or for battle. Isaiah says that the LORD "has bared his holy arm" before all the nations (Isaiah 52:10). Ezekiel acts out the LORD's power turned against the city.

decisions.choice: you will prophesy against it: words with the sign
decisions.reason: The signs are not silent: Ezekiel is to speak against the city too. His speaking is limited to what the LORD gives him (3:26-27).

decisions.choice: direct your face toward (L); turn to face (B); turn toward (R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 3. Readable says "ready for action" for what the bared arm means (m1).

decisions.choice: profetiza contra (every level)
decisions.reason: For the whole book (6:2; 11:4; 13:2, 17; 21:2; 25:2 and after): the command is "profetiza contra", the "tu" imperative God uses to Ezekiel, at every level, as the English keeps "prophesy against" (m2). The shared rules give it as "profetize contra"; with "tu" the imperative is "profetiza".

decisions.choice: nói tiên tri (L, B); truyền sứ điệp của Ta (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says what prophesying is here, the LORD's message, as the term sheet allows; it keeps "nói tiên tri" where the act itself is in view.

source.text: וְהִנֵּ֛ה נָתַ֥תִּי עָלֶ֖יךָ עֲבוֹתִ֑ים וְלֹֽא־תֵהָפֵ֤ךְ מִֽצִּדְּךָ֙ אֶל־צִדֶּ֔ךָ עַד־כַּלּוֹתְךָ֖ יְמֵ֥י מְצוּרֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And see, I will put on you ropes, and not you will turn from your side to your side until you have completed [the] days of your siege.

en.L: And see, I will put cords on you, and you will not turn from your side to your [other] side until you have completed the days of your siege.
en.B: I will tie you up with ropes so that you cannot turn from one side to the other until you have finished the days of your siege.
en.R: I will tie you up with ropes, so that you cannot turn over from one side to the other until you have finished the days of your attack on the city.

pt.L: E eis que porei cordas sobre ti, e não te virarás do teu lado para o teu [outro] lado até que tenhas completado os dias do teu cerco.
pt.B: Eu te amarrarei com cordas, de modo que não poderás te virar de um lado para o outro até terminares os dias do teu cerco.
pt.R: Vou te amarrar com cordas, para que não possas te virar de um lado para o outro até terminares os dias do teu ataque contra a cidade.

sw.L: Na tazama, nitakutia kamba, wala hutageuka kutoka upande wako kwenda upande wako [mwingine] hadi utakapozimaliza siku za kuzingira kwako.
sw.B: Nitakufunga kwa kamba ili usiweze kugeuka kutoka upande mmoja kwenda mwingine hadi utakapozimaliza siku za kuzingira kwako.
sw.R: Nitakufunga kwa kamba ili usiweze kujigeuza kutoka upande mmoja kwenda mwingine hadi utakapozimaliza siku za kuushambulia mji.

ko.L: 그리고 보라, 내가 너에게 줄을 씌울 것이니, 너는 네 포위의 날들을 마칠 때까지 이쪽에서 저쪽으로 돌아눕지 못할 것이다.
ko.B: 내가 너를 밧줄로 묶어서, 네가 포위하는 날들을 다 채울 때까지 이쪽에서 저쪽으로 돌아눕지 못하게 하겠다.
ko.R: 내가 너를 밧줄로 묶어서, 네가 그 성을 공격하는 날들이 다 끝날 때까지 이쪽에서 저쪽으로 돌아눕지 못하게 하겠다.

vi.L: Và kìa, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ đặt dây trên ngươi, và ngươi sẽ không trở mình từ bên này sang bên [kia] cho đến khi ngươi làm trọn những ngày vây hãm của ngươi.
vi.B: Ta sẽ lấy dây trói con lại, để con không thể trở mình từ bên này sang bên kia cho đến khi con làm trọn những ngày vây hãm.
vi.R: Ta sẽ trói con lại bằng dây, để con không thể trở mình từ bên này sang bên kia cho đến khi con làm xong những ngày tấn công thành.

fr.L: Et voici, je mettrai sur toi des cordes, et tu ne te tourneras pas de ton côté sur ton [autre] côté jusqu’à ce que tu aies achevé les jours de ton siège.
fr.B: Je t’attacherai avec des cordes, si bien que tu ne pourras pas te retourner d’un côté sur l’autre jusqu’à ce que tu aies achevé les jours de ton siège.
fr.R: Je t’attacherai avec des cordes, et tu ne pourras pas te retourner d’un côté sur l’autre avant d’avoir fini les jours de ton attaque contre la ville.

es.L: Y mira, pondré sobre ti cuerdas, y no te volverás de un lado a tu [otro] lado hasta que hayas cumplido los días de tu asedio.
es.B: Te ataré con cuerdas para que no puedas volverte de un lado al otro hasta que hayas cumplido los días de tu asedio.
es.R: Te ataré con cuerdas, para que no puedas darte la vuelta de un lado al otro hasta que hayas terminado los días de tu ataque contra la ciudad.

decisions.choice: I will put cords on you: the LORD binds Ezekiel
decisions.reason: Here the LORD himself puts the cords on Ezekiel (compare 3:25). He is held to his task until the days of the sign are complete, as the city will be held in the siege until its end.

decisions.choice: from one side to the other (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "from your side to your side". Balanced and Readable say it as English would. Readable says "your attack on the city" for "your siege", the siege Ezekiel acts out.

source.text: וְאַתָּ֣ה קַח־לְךָ֡ חִטִּ֡ין וּ֠שְׂעֹרִים וּפ֨וֹל וַעֲדָשִׁ֜ים וְדֹ֣חַן וְכֻסְּמִ֗ים וְנָתַתָּ֤ה אוֹתָם֙ בִּכְלִ֣י אֶחָ֔ד וְעָשִׂ֧יתָ אוֹתָ֛ם לְךָ֖ לְלָ֑חֶם מִסְפַּ֨ר הַיָּמִ֜ים אֲשֶׁר־אַתָּ֣ה׀שׁוֹכֵ֣ב עַֽל־צִדְּךָ֗ שְׁלֹשׁ־מֵא֧וֹת וְתִשְׁעִ֛ים י֖וֹם תֹּאכֲלֶֽנּוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And you, take for yourself wheat and barley and beans and lentils and millet and spelt, and put them in one vessel, and make them for yourself into bread; [the] number of the days which you [are] lying on your side, three hundred and ninety days, you will eat it.

en.L: And you, take for yourself wheat and barley and beans and lentils and millet and spelt, and place them in one vessel, and make them into bread for yourself; [for] the number of the days that you are lying on your side, 390 days, you will eat it.
en.B: Take wheat and barley, beans and lentils, millet and spelt. Put them in one container and make bread for yourself from them. You are to eat it during the 390 days that you lie on your side.
en.R: Take wheat, barley, beans, lentils, millet and spelt. Put them all in one bowl and make bread for yourself. Eat it during the 390 days that you lie on your side.

pt.L: E tu, toma para ti trigo, e cevada, e favas, e lentilhas, e painço, e espelta, e põe-nos numa só vasilha, e faz deles pão para ti; [pelo] número dos dias em que estiveres deitado sobre o teu lado, 390 dias, tu o comerás.
pt.B: Pega trigo e cevada, favas e lentilhas, painço e espelta. Coloca tudo numa só vasilha e faz pão para ti com eles. Tu o comerás durante os 390 dias em que ficares deitado sobre o teu lado.
pt.R: Pega trigo, cevada, favas, lentilhas, painço e espelta. Coloca tudo numa tigela e faz pão para ti. Come esse pão durante os 390 dias em que ficares deitado de lado.

sw.L: Nawe jitwalie ngano na shayiri na maharagwe na dengu na mtama na spelti, uviweke katika chombo kimoja, ujifanyie mkate kwa hivyo; [kwa] hesabu ya siku unazolala kwa upande wako, siku 390, utaula.
sw.B: Chukua ngano na shayiri, maharagwe na dengu, mtama na spelti. Viweke katika chombo kimoja, ujifanyie mkate kwa hivyo. Utaula katika siku zile 390 utakazolala kwa upande wako.
sw.R: Chukua ngano, shayiri, maharagwe, dengu, mtama na spelti. Viweke vyote katika bakuli moja ujitengenezee mkate. Ule mkate huo katika siku zile 390 utakazolala kwa upande wako.

ko.L: 그리고 너는 밀과 보리와 콩과 렌즈콩과 조와 스펠트밀을 가져다가 한 그릇에 담고, 그것들로 너를 위해 빵을 만들어라. 네가 옆으로 누워 있는 날 수, 곧 390일 동안 너는 그것을 먹어라.
ko.B: 밀과 보리, 콩과 렌즈콩, 조와 스펠트밀을 가져다가 한 그릇에 담고, 그것으로 너를 위해 빵을 만들어라. 네가 옆으로 누워 있는 390일 동안 그 빵을 먹어야 한다.
ko.R: 밀, 보리, 콩, 렌즈콩, 조, 스펠트밀을 가져다가 모두 한 그릇에 담고 빵을 만들어라. 네가 옆으로 누워 있는 390일 동안 그 빵을 먹어라.

vi.L: Và ngươi, hãy lấy cho mình lúa mì, lúa mạch, đậu, đậu lăng, hạt kê và lúa mì spen-tơ, và bỏ chúng vào một cái bình, và làm bánh cho mình bằng chúng; ngươi nằm nghiêng bao nhiêu ngày, 390 ngày, ngươi sẽ ăn bánh ấy.
vi.B: Hãy lấy lúa mì và lúa mạch, đậu và đậu lăng, hạt kê và lúa mì spen-tơ. Hãy bỏ chung vào một cái bình và làm bánh cho mình. Con phải ăn bánh ấy trong suốt 390 ngày con nằm nghiêng.
vi.R: Hãy lấy lúa mì, lúa mạch, đậu, đậu lăng, hạt kê và lúa mì spen-tơ. Hãy bỏ tất cả vào một cái tô và làm bánh cho mình. Hãy ăn bánh ấy trong suốt 390 ngày con nằm nghiêng.

fr.L: Et toi, prends-toi du blé, et de l’orge, et des fèves, et des lentilles, et du millet, et de l’épeautre, et mets-les dans un seul récipient, et fais-t’en du pain ; [pendant] le nombre de jours où tu seras couché sur ton côté, 390 jours, tu en mangeras.
fr.B: Prends du blé et de l’orge, des fèves et des lentilles, du millet et de l’épeautre. Mets-les dans un même récipient et fais-t’en du pain. Tu en mangeras pendant les 390 jours où tu resteras couché sur le côté.
fr.R: Prends du blé, de l’orge, des fèves, des lentilles, du millet et de l’épeautre. Mets tout dans un seul bol et fais-toi du pain. Mange-le pendant les 390 jours où tu resteras couché sur le côté.

es.L: Y tú, toma para ti trigo y cebada y habas y lentejas y mijo y espelta, y ponlos en una vasija, y hazte con ellos pan; [durante] el número de los días que estés acostado sobre tu lado, 390 días, lo comerás.
es.B: Toma trigo y cebada, habas y lentejas, mijo y espelta. Ponlos en un solo recipiente y hazte pan con ellos. Lo comerás durante los 390 días que estés acostado sobre tu lado.
es.R: Toma trigo, cebada, habas, lentejas, mijo y espelta. Ponlo todo en un tazón y hazte pan. Cómelo durante los 390 días que estés acostado sobre tu lado.

decisions.choice: wheat, barley, beans, lentils, millet and spelt: famine bread
decisions.reason: In a siege, when grain runs short, bread is made from whatever is left, mixed together in one jar. Beans and lentils were not normally used for bread. Spelt was a hardy kind of wheat (Exodus 9:32; Isaiah 28:25); the word for millet occurs only here.

decisions.choice: 390 days: as in verse 5
decisions.reason: The Greek translation reads 190 here too. See the note at verse 5. The bread is for the days on the left side; the forty days of verse 6 are not counted here.

decisions.choice: one container (B); one bowl (R)
decisions.reason: The word means any jar or vessel. Readable says "bowl", the picture of mixing; numbers over ninety-nine are in numerals at every level.

decisions.choice: spelti
decisions.reason: Spelt keeps its name as in the published Exodus 9:32.

decisions.choice: "렌즈콩", "조", "스펠트밀"
decisions.reason: The grains as the published Korean 2 Samuel 17:28 (렌즈콩) and Exodus 9:32 (스펠트밀) name them; millet is "조".

decisions.choice: lúa mì spen-tơ
decisions.reason: Spelt has no common Vietnamese name; the borrowed "spen-tơ" with "lúa mì" tells the reader it is a kind of wheat. A reviewer may prefer another word.

decisions.choice: "espelta"
decisions.reason: The published Spanish word for spelt (Exodus 9:32; Isaiah 28:25)

source.text: וּמַאֲכָֽלְךָ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תֹּאכֲלֶ֔נּוּ בְּמִשְׁק֕וֹל עֶשְׂרִ֥ים שֶׁ֖קֶל לַיּ֑וֹם מֵעֵ֥ת עַד־עֵ֖ת תֹּאכֲלֶֽנּוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And your food which you eat [will be] by weight, twenty shekels for the day; from time to time you will eat it.

en.L: And your food that you eat [will be] by weight, twenty shekels for the day; from time to time you will eat it.
en.B: The food you eat is to be weighed out, {{units:about 8 ounces|twenty shekels}} a day, and you are to eat it at set times.
en.R: You may eat only {{units:about 8 ounces|twenty shekels}} of this bread a day. Eat it at set times.

pt.L: E o teu alimento que comeres [será] por peso, vinte siclos por dia; de tempo em tempo o comerás.
pt.B: O alimento que comeres deverá ser pesado, {{units:cerca de 230 gramas|vinte siclos}} por dia, e deverás comê-lo em horas certas.
pt.R: Só poderás comer {{units:cerca de 230 gramas|vinte siclos}} desse pão por dia. Come-o em horas certas.

sw.L: Na chakula chako utakachokula [kitakuwa] kwa uzito, shekeli ishirini kwa siku; mara kwa mara utakila.
sw.B: Chakula utakachokula kitapimwa kwa uzito, {{units:karibu gramu 230|shekeli ishirini}} kwa siku, nawe utakila kwa nyakati maalumu.
sw.R: Utakula mkate huo {{units:karibu gramu 230|shekeli ishirini}} tu kwa siku. Ule kwa nyakati maalumu.

ko.L: 그리고 네가 먹을 음식은 무게를 달아서 하루에 이십 세겔씩이다. 너는 때를 정해 놓고 그것을 먹어라.
ko.B: 네가 먹을 음식은 무게를 달아서 하루에 {{units:약 230그램|이십 세겔}}씩 먹되, 정해진 때에 먹어야 한다.
ko.R: 너는 하루에 그 빵을 {{units:약 230그램|이십 세겔}}만 먹을 수 있다. 정해진 때에 먹어라.

vi.L: Và thức ăn ngươi ăn [sẽ được] cân, hai mươi siếc-lơ mỗi ngày; theo giờ nhất định ngươi sẽ ăn.
vi.B: Thức ăn con ăn phải được cân, {{units:khoảng 230 g|hai mươi siếc-lơ}} mỗi ngày, và con phải ăn vào những giờ nhất định.
vi.R: Mỗi ngày con chỉ được ăn {{units:khoảng 230 g|hai mươi siếc-lơ}} bánh ấy. Hãy ăn vào những giờ nhất định.

fr.L: Et ta nourriture que tu mangeras [sera] au poids, vingt sicles par jour ; de temps en temps tu en mangeras.
fr.B: La nourriture que tu mangeras sera pesée : {{units:environ 230 grammes|vingt sicles}} par jour, et tu la mangeras à heures fixes.
fr.R: Tu ne pourras manger que {{units:environ 230 grammes|vingt sicles}} de ce pain par jour. Mange-le à heures fixes.

es.L: Y tu comida que comas [será] por peso, veinte siclos al día; de tiempo en tiempo la comerás.
es.B: La comida que comas será pesada, {{units:unos 230 gramos|veinte siclos}} al día, y la comerás a horas fijas.
es.R: Solo podrás comer {{units:unos 230 gramos|veinte siclos}} de este pan al día. Cómelo a horas fijas.

decisions.choice: twenty shekels a day: a starvation ration
decisions.reason: A shekel was a weight of about two-fifths of an ounce, so twenty shekels was about eight ounces of bread a day, much less than a person needs. Food weighed out by the ounce is a sign of siege famine (verse 16; Leviticus 26:26).

decisions.choice: from time to time: at fixed times
decisions.reason: The phrase means at set intervals, probably once a day. The ration is measured and timed; there is no more.

decisions.choice: about 8 ounces / twenty shekels (units setting)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the shekels. Balanced and Readable give the modern weight, with the shekels as the alternative, as the published books do (ten shekels is about 4 ounces).

decisions.choice: cerca de 230 gramas / vinte siclos (units setting)
decisions.reason: For the whole book: measures are metric by default, with the Hebrew unit as the alternative, where the English gives US units; Literal keeps the unit, as the Old Testament terms set it. Twenty shekels at 11,5 g is about 230 g (m1); verse 11's sixth of a hin is about 0,6 litro.

decisions.choice: karibu gramu 230 / shekeli ishirini (units setting)
decisions.reason: Swahili gives modern measures in metric units, with the original measure as the setting's alternative, as the published books do; Literal keeps the shekels. A shekel is taken as about 11.5 grams, as in the published books, and a hin as about 3.7 litres (verse 11).

decisions.choice: {{units:약 230그램|이십 세겔}}: metric by default, the original unit as the alternative
decisions.reason: Korean converts measures to metric with the original unit as the alternative, as in Kings, Isaiah and Jeremiah, while the English converts to US units; a shekel is reckoned at 11.5 grams. Literal keeps the shekel.

decisions.choice: {{units:khoảng 230 g|hai mươi siếc-lơ}}
decisions.reason: Vietnamese gives metric measures by default, with the original unit as the setting's alternative, where the English gives US units; a shekel is reckoned at 11.5 g. Literal keeps the original unit. The same in verse 11 (a sixth of a hin, about 0.6 litre).

decisions.choice: {{units:environ 230 grammes|vingt sicles}}: metric by default, for the whole book
decisions.reason: French uses metric measures, so the default differs from the English "about 8 ounces"; a shekel is taken as about 11.5 grams, as in the published Pentateuch and the term sheet. The original unit stays as the alternative, and Literal keeps it.

decisions.choice: "unos 230 gramos" / "veinte siclos" (units setting)
decisions.reason: Worked out on the Pentateuch's shekel of about 11.5 grams, as the term sheet's table

source.text: וּמַ֛יִם בִּמְשׂוּרָ֥ה תִשְׁתֶּ֖ה שִׁשִּׁ֣ית הַהִ֑ין מֵעֵ֥ת עַד־עֵ֖ת תִּשְׁתֶּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And water by measure you will drink, [the] sixth of the hin; from time to time you will drink.

en.L: And water you will drink by measure, the sixth of a hin; from time to time you will drink [it].
en.B: You are also to drink water by measure, {{units:about 2/3 quart|a sixth of a hin}}, and drink it at set times.
en.R: You may drink only {{units:about 2/3 quart|a sixth of a hin}} of water a day. Drink it at set times.

pt.L: E água beberás por medida, a sexta parte de um him; de tempo em tempo [a] beberás.
pt.B: Também deverás beber água por medida, {{units:cerca de 0,6 litro|a sexta parte de um him}}, e bebê-la em horas certas.
pt.R: Só poderás beber {{units:cerca de 0,6 litro|a sexta parte de um him}} de água por dia. Bebe-a em horas certas.

sw.L: Na maji utakunywa kwa kipimo, sehemu ya sita ya hini; mara kwa mara utakunywa.
sw.B: Utakunywa pia maji kwa kipimo, {{units:karibu lita 0.6|sehemu ya sita ya hini}}, nawe utayanywa kwa nyakati maalumu.
sw.R: Utakunywa maji {{units:karibu lita 0.6|sehemu ya sita ya hini}} tu kwa siku. Uyanywe kwa nyakati maalumu.

ko.L: 그리고 물도 되어서 한 힌의 육분의 일을 마셔라. 너는 때를 정해 놓고 마셔라.
ko.B: 물도 되어서 {{units:약 0.6리터|한 힌의 육분의 일}}씩 마시되, 정해진 때에 마셔야 한다.
ko.R: 물은 하루에 {{units:약 0.6리터|한 힌의 육분의 일}}만 마실 수 있다. 정해진 때에 마셔라.

vi.L: Và ngươi sẽ uống nước theo lường, một phần sáu hin; theo giờ nhất định ngươi sẽ uống.
vi.B: Con cũng phải uống nước theo lường, {{units:khoảng 0,6 lít|một phần sáu hin}}, và uống vào những giờ nhất định.
vi.R: Mỗi ngày con chỉ được uống {{units:khoảng 0,6 lít|một phần sáu hin}} nước. Hãy uống vào những giờ nhất định.

fr.L: Et tu boiras de l’eau à la mesure, le sixième d’un hin ; de temps en temps tu [en] boiras.
fr.B: Tu boiras aussi de l’eau mesurée, {{units:environ 0,6 litre|un sixième de hin}}, et tu la boiras à heures fixes.

decisions.choice: a sixth of a hin: about two-thirds of a quart
decisions.reason: A hin was a liquid measure of about a gallon, so a sixth of a hin was about two-thirds of a quart, less than a person needs in a day in a hot climate. Water too will run out in the siege (verse 16).

decisions.choice: about 2/3 quart / a sixth of a hin (units setting)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the hin. Balanced and Readable give the modern measure, with the hin as the alternative, as the published books give a hin as about a gallon. Readable adds "a day", which "from time to time" implies (verse 10).

decisions.choice: a barley cake baked on human dung: food made unclean
decisions.reason: A barley cake was a round, flat loaf baked on hot stones or embers (1 Kings 19:6). Dried animal dung was a common fuel for such fires, but the Law required human excrement to be buried outside the camp, because the LORD walked in its midst (Deuteronomy 23:13-15). Bread baked over it is unclean. The LORD explains the sign in verse 13.

decisions.choice: before their eyes: in public view
decisions.reason: Like the other signs, this one is done where the exiles can see it.

decisions.choice: dung of human excrement (L); human dung (B, R)
decisions.reason: The words are plain in the Hebrew, and every level keeps them plain, without coarseness and without a softer word that would hide the point (m1). Readable adds "as fuel" to explain the baking. The quotation mark closes the speech that began in 3:24.

decisions.choice: um bolo de cevada (L); um pão de cevada (B); um pão achatado de cevada (R)
decisions.reason: The flat round loaf (m1) is "bolo" at Literal, the old Bible word, but Brazilian "bolo" now means a sweet cake, so Balanced and Readable say "pão", and Readable adds "achatado", as the English Readable says "flat". The dung is named plainly at every level, as the English does (r-en-1).

decisions.choice: they will eat their bread unclean among the nations: exile makes everything unclean
decisions.reason: In the land, the people could keep the food laws and bring their offerings to the LORD's house. In a foreign land, away from the temple, their food would be unclean (Hosea 9:3-4; Amos 7:17). The sign of the unclean bread shows the exile as a life cut off from the LORD's presence.

decisions.choice: the Israelites / the sons of Israel (gender setting)

en.L: And I said, "Ah, Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}! See, my soul has not been made unclean; and what dies [of itself] and what is torn I have not eaten from my youth until now, and no foul meat has come into my mouth."
en.B: Then I said, "Oh, Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}! I have never made myself unclean. From my youth until now I have never eaten anything that died by itself or was torn by wild animals, and no spoiled sacrificial meat has ever entered my mouth."
en.R: Then I said, "Oh no, Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}! I have never made myself unclean. Since I was young, I have never eaten meat from an animal that died by itself or was killed by wild animals. I have never put any unclean meat in my mouth."

vi.R: Bấy giờ tôi thưa: "Ôi, lạy Chúa là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}! Con chưa hề làm cho mình bị ô uế. Từ khi còn nhỏ, con chưa hề ăn thịt con vật tự chết hay bị thú dữ giết. Con chưa hề để thịt ô uế nào vào miệng."

fr.L: Et je dis : « Ah ! Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} ! Voici, mon âme n’a pas été rendue impure ; et bête morte et bête déchirée, je n’en ai pas mangé depuis ma jeunesse jusqu’à maintenant, et aucune viande avariée n’est entrée dans ma bouche. »
fr.B: Alors je dis : « Ah ! Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} ! Je ne me suis jamais rendu impur. Depuis ma jeunesse jusqu’à maintenant, je n’ai jamais mangé d’une bête morte d’elle-même ou déchirée par les fauves, et aucune viande de sacrifice avariée n’est jamais entrée dans ma bouche. »
fr.R: Alors j’ai dit : « Oh non, Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} ! Je ne me suis jamais rendu impur. Depuis que je suis jeune, je n’ai jamais mangé la viande d’un animal mort tout seul ou tué par des bêtes sauvages. Je n’ai jamais mis de viande impure dans ma bouche. »

es.L: Y dije: «¡Ah, Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}! Mira, mi alma no ha sido contaminada; y animal muerto [por sí mismo] o despedazado no he comido desde mi juventud hasta ahora, y nunca ha entrado en mi boca carne corrompida».
es.B: Entonces dije: «¡Ay, Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}! Yo nunca me he contaminado. Desde mi juventud hasta ahora nunca he comido nada que muriera por sí solo o que fuera despedazado por las fieras, y nunca ha entrado en mi boca carne de sacrificio corrompida».
es.R: Entonces dije: «¡Oh no, Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}! Yo nunca me he hecho impuro. Desde que era joven, nunca he comido carne de un animal que muriera solo o que fuera matado por las fieras. Nunca me he puesto en la boca carne impura».

decisions.choice: what dies of itself, what is torn, foul meat: the meat the Law forbids
decisions.reason: The Law forbids eating an animal that has died by itself or been killed by wild animals (Exodus 22:30; Leviticus 17:15), and priests most of all (Leviticus 22:8; Ezekiel 44:31). "Foul meat" is the meat of a sacrifice left too long, which had become unclean (Leviticus 7:18; 19:7). Ezekiel the priest has kept himself clean all his life.

decisions.choice: Ah, Lord GOD! my soul has not been made unclean: Ezekiel's only protest
decisions.reason: This is the one place where Ezekiel objects to a command. Peter's protest in Acts 10:14, "I have never eaten anything common or unclean", is much like it.

decisions.choice: Ah, Lord GOD (L); Oh, Lord GOD (B); Oh no, Lord GOD (R)
decisions.reason: The cry is worded as Jeremiah 1:6. Balanced and Readable say "myself" for "my soul", which here means the whole person, and "spoiled sacrificial meat" (B) and "unclean meat" (R) for "foul meat" (m1).

decisions.choice: Ah, Senhor DEUS! (L, B); Ah, não, Senhor DEUS! (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book (also 9:8; 11:13; 21:5): Ezekiel's cry to God takes the words Jeremiah 1:6 sets in Portuguese, "Ah, Senhor DEUS!", with Readable adding "não" as the English Readable adds "no"; one cry serves where the English varies "Ah" and "Oh". Ezekiel speaks to God with "tu". Balanced's "nunca entrou na minha boca" is the wording Acts 10:14 gives Peter's like protest (m2).

decisions.choice: Ole wangu, Bwana MUNGU! (L); Ee Bwana MUNGU! (B); Hapana, Bwana MUNGU! (R)
decisions.reason: Ezekiel's cry of dismay (also 9:8; 11:13; 21:5) takes the wording of the published Jeremiah 1:6 at each level, as the terms note sets it.

decisions.choice: "아, $LG!" with the bare name as vocative, and Ezekiel speaks to God in 합쇼체 with "저"
decisions.reason: A prophet speaks to God in 합쇼체; as a vocative the Lord GOD span takes no particle, because 이여/여 would read wrongly after one of its two forms (Jeremiah 1:6).

decisions.choice: Ôi, lạy Chúa là CHÚA!
decisions.reason: Ezekiel's cry as Jeremiah 1:6 publishes it, at every level; the same in 9:8, 11:13 and 21:5. Ezekiel calls himself "con" when he speaks to God.

decisions.choice: "Ah ! Seigneur DIEU !" (Literal, Balanced); "Oh non, Seigneur DIEU !" (Readable), for the whole book
decisions.reason: The term sheet's wording for this cry, as the published Jeremiah 1:6.

decisions.choice: "¡Ah, Señor DIOS!" (L); "¡Ay, Señor DIOS!" (B); "¡Oh no, Señor DIOS!" (R)
decisions.reason: Book-wide wording of Ezekiel's cry, as Jeremiah 1:6 in Spanish

decisions.choice: I am breaking the staff of bread ... bread by weight: the curse of Leviticus 26:26
decisions.reason: Bread is the staff that supports life. Leviticus 26:26 warns that if Israel breaks the covenant, the LORD will "break the staff of bread", and bread will be handed out by weight. Ezekiel's rations in verses 10-11 act out this curse, and the same phrase returns in 5:16 and 14:13. Much of chapters 4-5 echoes Leviticus 26.

decisions.choice: with anxiety ... with horror: the fear of starvation
decisions.reason: The two words describe the mood of a starving city: worry over every mouthful, and dismay as the food and water run out.

decisions.choice: break the staff of bread (L, B); take away the food supply (R)
decisions.reason: As in Leviticus 26:26. The verse runs on into verse 17 at Literal and Balanced.

decisions.choice: quebrar o bordão do pão (L, B); tirar o alimento de que ... depende (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book (also 5:16; 14:13): the curse of Leviticus 26:26 (m1) takes the words Leviticus has in Portuguese, "o bordão do pão", the staff one leans on, at Literal and Balanced; Readable gives its sense, as Leviticus 26:26 does at Readable. Verse 17's "apodrecerão na sua iniquidade" (L) and "definharão" (B, R) follow Leviticus 26:39 likewise.
